item.title: Tender Brief — Part 1: Wildfire Evidence Review, Pilot-Area Recommendation and Part 2 Commissioning Brief
item.description:
Advertised value: GBP 25,000 Status: active Deadline: 2026-12-21T12:00:00+00:00
Ffermio Bro is a Farming in Protected Landscapes Scheme that supports farmers working collaboratively to deliver ecosystem resilience. Ffermio Bro’s first objective is to support ecosystems and restore nature. Ffermio Bro’s secondary objectives are to support measures that protect and enhance heritage features, improve access and mitigate the risks of Wildfires. In an ever-changing climate, wildfire planning and mitigation is more important now than ever. Eryri National Park Authority (ENPA) is seeking to appoint a consultant to undertake Part 1 of a two-stage wildfire risk management project. This tender covers Part 1 only. Part 1 — Evidence gathering, pilot-area recommendation and preparation of a commissioning brief: The consultant will gather and analyse evidence on wildfire risk and potential prevention across Eryri, review relevant good practice, recommend a suitable pilot area and prepare a commissioning brief for Part 2. Part 2 — Preparation of a pilot-area wildfire prevention plan: Under a separate future commission, a consultant will use the findings of Part 1 to prepare a wildfire prevention plan for the selected pilot area, an integrated, adaptable plan that can be replicated across other areas within the National Park. Preparing that plan is not included in this tender. The overarching objectives of this work is to: • Develop an evidence base to inform decisions on wildfire prevention across Eryri. • Provide evidence on what actions work to mitigate wildfire and how to implement these mitigations in comparable vegetation, landscape and climatic conditions. • Analyse and present which approaches to wildfire risk management have been successful for organisations, communities and individuals, and why. • Identify needs, risks and opportunities for action, including practical essentials such as access and water supplies. • Recommend a pilot area for the work, supported by a clear justification using the evidence researched for the selection, then; prepare a commissioning brief for a wildfire prevention and management plan for the pilot area. • Identify what capital expenditure to prioritise investment for ENPA in the short (<1 year), medium (1 to3 years) and long term (3 years+)
